citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., & He, J. (2023). C-E VAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023).
creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He (Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)
description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13,948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels and 52 diverse disciplines.
name: C-EVAL
publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors of the paper (researchers and students from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and HKUST).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The questions undergo several rounds of human validation by the authors, and all the LATEX notations are ensured to be complied without syntax errors.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed – automatically when possible, and otherwise manually by the authors – into a structured format. For subjects with complex mathematical notations, they are manually converted into standard LATEX formats. Questions with fewer than four options are eliminated, and incorrect choices are randomly dropped for questions with more than four options.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is designed to mitigate the geographical biases of English benchmarks by focusing on Chinese users' primary interests, such as Chinese culture, history, and laws, as well as other competencies unique in Chinese society.
rai:dataCollection: The primary source of data is mock exams freely available on the internet. In addition, a portion of the college-level questions are past exam questions from top universities in China, publicly shared by students. A minor fraction of college questions are mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam, sourced from the Weipu website.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The collected data come in various formats, primarily as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages.
rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL, along with all the English-language benchmarks, is far from perfect for LLM evaluation. There are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options are eliminated, and incorrect choices are randomly dropped for questions with more than four options.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents are initially processed into text. All questions are subsequently parsed into a structured format. Complex mathematical notations are manually converted into standard LATEX formats. All questions go through a standard data preprocessing pipeline, such as deduplication and cleaning.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors hope C-EVAL could guide developers to understand the abilities of their models from multiple dimensions and facilitate the growth of foundation models for Chinese users.
rai:dataUseCases: To assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was prompted to generate step-by-step explanations to explain the ground-truth answers, which were then manually revised.
